review_notes:
I read all of lines 1–192. The file has no simp lemmas, no @[simp] attributes, no simp sets and no local simp instances. It contains three theorems: the real joint tilted cutoff bound, its complex variant, and the exceptional-matrix theorem.

The only simp-related code is in proofs:
- The `simpa only [← Complex.ofReal_mul, ← Complex.ofReal_tsum, ← Complex.ofReal_sub, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs]` call converts the complex hypothesis into the real one. The reversed cast lemmas are used deliberately, for one targeted `simpa only` rewrite. They are not registered globally, so they cannot create a competing rule or a cycle.
- `simpa only [Fintype.card_fin]` and `simpa only [one_mul, Function.comp_def]` are small, targeted uses.

I did not find a missing canonical simp lemma, a wrongly oriented rule, competing rules or an unwanted expansion. Adding simp annotations to these large-hypothesis theorems would not help. I did not read the imported files in detail, because the target declares no simp interface of its own. I have no evidence of a simp-interface problem.
